summary: Reap stdio hosts when worker startup fails

delivery.outcome: Reap an already spawned stdio host and close its pipes when the worker thread cannot start; preserve the original startup exception and cache/retry semantics.
nonGoals: No claim about the original intermittent timing cause
No deadline, assertion, dependency, function, protocol or release changes
Preserve peer030 generation repair and all foreign workspaces

architecture.decision: Retain existing process-group cleanup and bounded wait/join. On worker.start failure use existing close lifecycle, close pipes synchronously for a never-started worker, and re-raise the original exception. Add real-subprocess failure injection and successful recovery controls.
architecture.rollback: Reviewed revert of constructor cleanup and its regression only.

validation.evidence: A real child process leaks before the repair on injected thread-start failure; after the repair it is reaped, both pipes close, cache stays empty, original exception survives and a subsequent healthy request succeeds without replay.
All existing assertions, host lifecycle controls and the peer027 path regressions remain valid.
Pinned networkless runtime verifies HTTP/gRPC/stdio, persistence and MCP with the original generated function unchanged.
Author delivery, exact-head required checks, independent review and protected merge; no manual merge or release.
